\section[la vacante]{la vacante — the vacancy, the open post}

\label{lesson:ES-C590-vacante}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for not at all, then the Spanish for deep down.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la vacante}
\textbf{la vacante} — \textquotedblleft{}the vacancy, the open post\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Hay una vacante en la tienda.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{There is a vacancy in the shop.}
\end{quote}

Also an adjective: \emph{un puesto vacante}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{vacante} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{vacans} 'being empty', from \emph{vacare} 'to be empty, to be free' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la vacante}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la vacante}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la vacante}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for not at all, then the Spanish for deep down, then say \emph{la vacante} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la vacante mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The vacancy, the open post\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[seleccionar]{seleccionar — to select, to choose}

\label{lesson:ES-C590-seleccionar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for deep down, then the Spanish for the vacancy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: seleccionar}
\textbf{seleccionar} — \textquotedblleft{}to select, to choose\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Seleccionamos a tres personas para la entrevista.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We selected three people for the interview.}
\end{quote}

More formal than \emph{elegir}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{seleccionar} is built on \emph{selección}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{selectio} 'a picking out' (EtymDB), from \emph{seligere}, built on \emph{legere} 'to gather'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{seleccionar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{seleccionar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{seleccionar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for deep down, then the Spanish for the vacancy, then say \emph{seleccionar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does seleccionar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To select, to choose\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[el empleado]{el empleado — the employee}

\label{lesson:ES-C590-empleado}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the vacancy, then the Spanish for to select.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el empleado}
\textbf{el empleado} — \textquotedblleft{}the employee\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Es empleado de un banco.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He is a bank employee.}
\end{quote}

A woman is \emph{la empleada}; in Spain \emph{la empleada del hogar} is a domestic worker.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{empleado} is the participle of \emph{emplear}, which was borrowed from Old French \emph{empleier}, from Latin \emph{implicare} 'to fold in, to involve' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el empleado}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el empleado}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el empleado}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the vacancy, then the Spanish for to select, then say \emph{el empleado} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el empleado mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The employee\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[la formación]{la formación — the training, the education}

\label{lesson:ES-C590-formacion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to select, then the Spanish for the employee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la formación}
\textbf{la formación} — \textquotedblleft{}the training, the education\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Buscamos a alguien con formación técnica.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We are looking for someone with technical training.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Formación profesional} (FP) is vocational training in Spain.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{formación} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{formatio} 'a shaping', built on \emph{formare} and \emph{forma} 'shape' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la formación}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la formación}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to select, then the Spanish for the employee, then say \emph{la formación} again
\end{itemize}

\section[el perfil]{el perfil — the profile}

\label{lesson:ES-C590-perfil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the employee, then the Spanish for the training.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el perfil}
\textbf{el perfil} — \textquotedblleft{}the profile\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Buscamos un perfil técnico.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We are looking for someone with a technical profile.}
\end{quote}

In a job offer it is the kind of person wanted. \emph{Mi perfil} is also your profile online.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{perfil} was borrowed from Occitan \emph{perfil} 'outline' (EtymDB), usually traced to Latin \emph{filum} 'thread': a line drawn round the edge.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
